maya: Heads-up — CI run for new quantized llama-variant showing nondeterministic token drift after resume. Not a perf crash, just output skew.
ashwin: Ugh. Can you paste the minimal repro?
maya: Steps: start eval runner (batch size 8) -> terminate at step ~120 -> resume from checkpoint -> same seed -> different tokens after ~token 10. Repro on local and CI sometimes, intermittent.
zhou: Seen similar once with mixed-kernel quant builds. Hypothesis: RNG state not restored exactly on resume due to sharded KV cache offsets.
omar: I captured a short log snippet from CI run: 
```
[runner] resuming checkpoint ckpt/2026-03-01-1200 id=ckpt_42 seed=12345
[model] restored kvcache shards=4 worker=2 offset=96
[sampler] initial_rng_state_sha1=3f7a...
[decode] step=9 token=42 prob=0.12 top_p=0.92 rng_sample=0.0078 -> token=42
[decode] step=10 token=17 prob=0.04 top_p=0.90 rng_sample=0.0035 -> token=17
[decode] step=11 token=5 prob=0.02 top_p=0.88 rng_sample=0.0024 -> token=5
-- resume later --
[decode] step=11 token=6 prob=0.019 top_p=0.88 rng_sample=0.0021 -> token=6  # divergence here
```
omar: rng_sample differs by a small amount and that flips the sample at step 11.
sophie: Did you check whether the RNG stream is advanced by KV cache restores or per-shard warmup?
maya: Not yet, but my patch to debug injected counters for number of rng draws per-worker and per-checkpoint: saw counts off by 7 on worker 2 after restore.
ashwin: That would explain deterministic offset. If different workers draw different numbers pre-resume, then after resume the global seed alignment is off. Top-p is sensitive to small rng deltas.
zhou: Quick idea: add an explicit rng-position metadata field to checkpoint that records total draws so far, and on resume call rng.advance(draws) before continuing. Also guard by per-worker offsets for sharding.
maya: I tried a prototype: added ckpt.rng_draws and runner.restore() calls rng.advance(ckpt.rng_draws_per_worker[worker_id]). On local, this removed token skew in simple cases. But CI still flakes sometimes.
omar: Could still be race: some workers restore slightly later and perform internal warmup draws (e.g., attention-prime) before we apply advance. Need deterministic order: restore rng -> restore kvcache -> apply advances -> then warmup without drawing.
ashwin: Agreed. Also quant kernels may do small stochastic bookkeeping draws (for numeric accumulation?). We should audit all modules for any implicit RNG usage during restore.
sophie: Another angle: top_p rounding/normalization differences between quantized logits and float logits could change tail mass. Even with perfect RNG alignment, quant noise can push cumulative prob over threshold earlier.
zhou: Good point — I ran an ablation: disable top_p sampling and use top_k=1 deterministic on resumed runs => no divergence. That suggests sampling threshold interplay with numeric noise.
maya: For immediate CI relief I propose: 1) persist rng_draws_per_worker in checkpoint, 2) apply advance early in restore path before any warmup ops, 3) add unit test that simulates resume+sampling across sharded workers, 4) add telemetry that logs rng_draws and kvcache_offsets to tracing.
nashwin: Sounds solid. Can you open a PR with prototype patch and a failing test? Put the test under eval_runner/tests/test_resume_determinism.py and mark it flaky-on-ci with @flaky until fixed.
maya: Will do. PR will include a small patch in runner/restore.py: 
```
# pseudo
ck = load_ckpt(path)
for w in workers:
  w.rng = RandomState(ck.seed)
  w.rng.advance(ck.rng_draws_per_worker[w.id])
  w.restore_kv(ck.kv_shard[w.id])
```
I'll also add a guard to run advance before any restore side-effect.
omar: For CI reproducibility please record full traces of rng sha1, rng_draws, kv_offsets in the post-run artifact. That will help triage intermittent failures.
deploy-bot: CI run 2026-03-18T14:12:03 finished — artifacts: s3://redwood-ci/2234567890/
ci-bot: Noted. Triggering nightly deterministic-smoke job with resume-path and logging enabled.
sophie: One more future thought: implement a compact 'entropy watermark' value in checkpoint that is the RNG internal counter diff + a checksum of kvcache numeric state. If resume checksum mismatches, fail fast and rerun full cold-start to ensure deterministic baseline.
maya: Nice. I'll prototype watermark in the PR too.
nashwin: Thanks team. If we get the unit test stable we can roll checkpoint metadata change behind a feature flag for Dedicated customers.
maya: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/eval-runner/pull/462 — tests + telemetry. Asking reviewers @zhou @ashwin.
zhou: Reviewing now. Quick scan looks reasonable, will run local smoke.
omar: I'll try reproducing the CI artifact locally with the same checkpoint and report back.
maya: Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
